title: Powdery Mildew on Cowpea, African eggplant and Pumpkin

Header: Powdery Mildew on Cowpea, African eggplant and Pumpkin

Prevention: Plant in sites with good air circulation and sun exposure.
Prune overcrowded plant material to help increase air circulation, recommended spacing of 2-3m.
Plant resistant varieties when available (ask local seller).
Clean field tools regularly after use.
Avoid late-season applications of nitrogen fertilizer to limit the production of succulent tissue, which is more susceptible to infection.
Avoid overhead watering to help reduce the relative humidity.
Remove and destroy all infected plant parts (leaves, etc.) by burning or burying 50 cm below ground.
Do not use crop remains as compost manure.
Monitoring: Look out for white to greyish powder like spots on stems, leaves and small branches.
The symptoms are common on the upper sides of the leaves though also appears on the lower leaves, young stems, flowers & young fruits.
Infected leaves curl and become distorted.
Leaves turn yellow with small spots of green.
Consider direct control when 6-10 plants out of 100 are displaying symptoms.
Direct Control: Sprays of potassium bicarbonate or sulphur based products will often control the disease.
Do not use collected leaves for composting.
Remove and destroy infected plant parts by burning/burying.
Water the crop early in the day at the root zone.
Add 4 cups of water and stir in few drops of soap.
Dilute 1 part of this filtrate with 9 parts of water.
Add 20 g of ginger powder to 1 litre of water.
Soak 50 g of finely shredded leaves in 1 litre of water.
Add 2 -3 litres and 10 ml soap as adhesive.
Restrictions: When using pesticides, wear protective clothing.
Follow instructions on product label (e.g. dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval etc.)
Do not empty into drains as chemicals can be toxic to aquatic organisms.
